newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kirch wants to oust Premiere chief - report.
newsitem.headline: Kirch wants to oust Premiere chief - report.

text.p: Bavarian media mogul Leo Kirch is trying to force the head of pay television group Premiere to resign, alleging that Bernd Kundrun has too often sided with Kirch arch-rival Bertelsmann AG, a magazine report said on Saturday.

Kirch lawyer Joachim Theye asked other Premiere shareholders -- Bertelsmann and French pay TV group Canal Plus -- to support relieving Kundrun of his duties, the weekly news magazine Der Spiegel said in an advance report released ahead of publication on Monday.

The magazine said that Bertelsmann and Canal Plus rejected the proposal on Friday and instead gave their full backing to Kundrun, who has turned Premiere from a slow-starter into a fast-growing channel with 1.41 million subscribers.
None of the companies were available for comment.
Kirch owns around 25 percent of Premiere, but the remaining shares are held equally by Bertelsmann and Canal Plus, who have sided together against Kirch in key developments at Premiere.

In a move to pursue his own business interests last year, Kirch set up a pay TV channel to rival Premiere called DF1 that broadcasts digital pay TV, a new technology allowing more channels and CD-like quality.
That set off a battle not only between Kirch and Bertelsmann, but also between Kirch and Premiere, the company he helped build and is now competing against.
The situation has developed into a messy court battle.

Premiere is suing Kirch for breach of faith. It argues that Kirch has a responsibility to remain loyal to the company, but since starting DF1 Kirch, who own substantial film rights, has withheld feature films from Premiere to show on DF1.

Last week, Kirch suffered a setback as a result of another suit by Premiere. The Hamburg-based pay TV group won an injunction against DF1, blocking Kirch's pay TV company from selling services outside of the state of Bavaria.
Premiere has also been beefing up its sports programming with the help of Bertelsmann, a direct challenge not only to DF1 but also to Kirch's struggling sports channel DSF.

In December, Premiere obtained the rights to live broadcasts of European Champions League soccer from the German TV station RTL, which is owned by Luxembourg-based media giant CLT/Ufa, which in turn is 50 percent owned by Bertelsmann.
